findings.description: check() used to return a bool, where True meant within policy. It now returns list[str] of violations, where an empty list means within policy. The truthiness test on line 26 is unchanged, so a report with no violations (empty list, falsy) is sent to NEEDS_REVIEW, and a report with violations (non-empty list, truthy) is auto-APPROVED. Every compliant report now waits for a manager and every non-compliant report is approved without review, which is a financial control failure.
findings.suggestion: Test for emptiness explicitly: `if not check(report, rates):` (or `problems = check(report, rates)` and branch on `if problems:`).
findings.title: decide() inverts the policy result because check() now returns a list
